purpose: Machine-readable API index for Ginject framework

public_surface.source_of_truth: api/ginject.txt (make api writes it, make api-check diffs it); design 0017
public_surface.note: The packages below are documented by their internal name (core, ctx, common, aggregation, versioning live under internal/); applications reach them only through the root aliases. log.Logger and log.LogAdapter moved from common to log.

core.responsibility: Application lifecycle, server, handler invocation, DI container (user docs: README.md; maintainer docs: internal/core/README.md)

App.description: Main application container; every core.New() is independent (own routes, providers, layers, logger, publisher)

methods.name: Create
methods.purpose: Wire the module tree, plan handlers, run OnReady (call once; panics on misuse)

methods.name: Listen
methods.purpose: Serve HTTP/1.1 (and h2c with IsH2C) on :port; nil opts = safe defaults; blocks until shut down

methods.name: ListenTLS
methods.signature: ListenTLS(port int, certFile, keyFile string, opts *ServerOptions) error
methods.purpose: Serve TLS with HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2; empty file names need opts.TLSConfig with certificates

methods.name: Serve
methods.purpose: Serve on a listener you made (TLS when opts.TLSConfig is set)

methods.name: Stop
methods.purpose: Graceful shutdown (drain, then OnShutdown hooks once); safe from any goroutine; from a handler use go app.Stop()

methods.name: ServeHTTP
methods.purpose: App is an http.Handler (advanced: no server defaults, no graceful shutdown)

methods.name: Get
methods.purpose: The instance this app created for p's type, nil before Create or for an unknown type

methods.name: SetLogger
methods.purpose: The one way to set the logger (before Create; nil panics)

methods.name: BindGlobalGuards
methods.purpose: Guards for every route and event

methods.name: BindGlobalInterceptors
methods.purpose: Interceptors for every route and event

methods.name: BindGlobalExceptionFilters
methods.purpose: Exception filters for every route and event

methods.name: EnableWS
methods.purpose: Enable WebSocket support with handshake middlewares

methods.name: EnableDevtool
methods.purpose: Devtool snapshot of routes and layers

methods.name: EnableAccessLog
methods.purpose: One access log line per request (the tracer's only listener)

notes: Configuration methods panic after Create: 'invalid app: <Method> must be called before Create'.

The request body cap is ServerOptions.MaxRequestBodyBytes of the serving call (0 = 10 MiB, negative = off); ServeHTTP wraps a body (not nil / http.NoBody) in http.MaxBytesReader. Exceeding it is a 413 exception from ctx.Body(). No SetMaxBodySize-style method exists.

Server timeouts are internal defaults, not options: ReadHeaderTimeout 5 s, ReadTimeout 30 s, WriteTimeout 30 s, IdleTimeout 75 s, MaxHeaderBytes 64 KiB. Deeper tuning: run App as an http.Handler in your own http.Server.
The logger API is SetLogger(l) and Logger() only; App has no exported fields.

Module.description: Composition root for controllers and providers with lifecycle hooks; fields set on the built module
fields: Name string - resolved by Build from the variable or function name (<package>.<name>); used in the InstanceLoader log line
IsGlobal bool - makes providers available to every module without an explicit import
OnInit func() - called during app.Create(), a module after the modules it imports, then its providers are constructed
OnReady func() - called once per app at the end of app.Create(), in the OnInit order
OnShutdown func() - called on graceful shutdown (SIGINT/SIGTERM, or app.Stop()), in the exact reverse of the OnInit order
methods: Prefix(prefix string) *Module - path prefix for the module's routes and its imports' routes
ID() string - identifier given by Build

ModuleBuilder.description: Fluent API for building modules: core.NewModuleBuilder() (ginject.ModuleBuilder()) returns a new *core.ModuleBuilder
ModuleBuilder.notes: No Export or IsGlobal builder methods exist: set m.IsGlobal on the built module.

ServerOptions.description: Options of Listen, ListenTLS and Serve; nil = defaults
fields: ShutdownTimeout time.Duration - drain time at shutdown (0 or negative = 30 s)
MaxRequestBodyBytes int64 - body cap (0 = 10 MiB, negative = off)
TLSConfig *tls.Config - ListenTLS / Serve TLS config, cloned
IsH2C bool - Listen / Serve without TLS also accept unencrypted HTTP/2

Controller.description: Any struct implementing NewController() Controller; embeds common.HTTP and/or common.WS

ctx.responsibility: Request context objects and dependency types

methods: Status(code int) *HTTPContext - sets the status code; chain with JSON/Text
JSON(data any, args ...any) - string = raw JSON, JSONAppender = own bytes, else encoding/json; encode error panics 500 and writes nothing
JSONP(data any, args ...any) - sanitized callback, nosniff, falls back to JSON
Body() Body - lazily parses JSON body; on http.MaxBytesError panics exception.RequestEntityTooLargeException (413), not a raw error
HTTPContext.notes: No SetDeadline()/IsDeadlineExceeded()/Deadline field exist on HTTPContext — do not invent per-request deadline APIs. See metadata-concurrency-model.json's cancellation_handling for the real (server-level-only) timeout model.

common.responsibility: Pipeline interfaces and embedded controller types
notes: Guards, interceptors and exception filters are bound as `any` (no named type), NOT compile-time Go interfaces. Shape is checked at bind time by method name and signature (a type assertion to an unexported interface, then the method value; no reflection per call) against the func-type aliases below. A layer bound to a method that is not a handler of the controller panics at Create(). A bound value missing the method panics with a *ShapeError (GuardShapeError / InterceptorShapeError / ExceptionFilterShapeError).
MiddlewareFn IS a real interface (requires a Use method) — different from the other three.

interfaces.MiddlewareFn: interface { Use(*http.Request, http.ResponseWriter, ctx.Next) } — real interface; Use = func(*http.Request, http.ResponseWriter, ctx.Next) is the matching func alias
interfaces.guard: any; checked against HTTPCanActivate = func(*ctx.HTTPContext) bool via method name "CanActivate"
interfaces.interceptor: any; checked against HTTPIntercept = func(*ctx.HTTPContext, *aggregation.Aggregation) any via method name "Intercept"
interfaces.exception filter: any; checked against HTTPCatch = func(*ctx.HTTPContext, *exception.Exception) via method name "Catch" — NOTE: HTTPContext is the FIRST parameter, Exception is SECOND
interfaces.Logger: interface { Debug(msg string, args ...any); Info(...); Warn(...); Error(...); Fatal(...) } — no Log()/LogStructured() methods exist
interfaces.Publisher: interface { Publish(topic string, payload ...any) error } — payload is variadic, not a single `data any`

embedded_types.HTTP: Embed in controller to enable HTTP routing (there is NO common.REST type — do not generate it)
embedded_types.WS: Embed in controller to enable WebSocket routing
embedded_types.Middleware: Separate embeddable type providing BindMiddleware(MiddlewareFn, ...any) *Middleware — not a field on HTTP/WS

notes: Router.Match signature is func (r *Router) Match(method, path, version string, params []string) (*RouterItem, []string): nil on a miss; the item is shared and read-only; the slice is params plus one value per route parameter (design 0002). Router.Group does not exist.
Route parameters are {name} whole segments (READ_BY_ID routes to GET /{ID}: the parameter name keeps the case of the method name); there is no :id syntax.

Exception.notes: No GetStackTrace()/SetStackTrace() and no stack-trace field exist. Exception{message, description, cause, code, isJoined} holds no prebuilt error; Error() derives the text. AppendJSON / MarshalJSON write {"code","error","message"} with encoding/json.

trace.tracer: type Tracer (zero value ready): Enabled() bool, Emit(Event), Listen(func(Event)) (stop func()); synchronous, no recover, 0 allocs. There is no event bus. core keeps one Tracer per app, unexported: EnableAccessLog() adds its only listener.
trace.notes: No "handshake" stage exists. Interceptor is split into pre_interceptor/post_interceptor (two constants), not one combined "interceptor". Exception filter stage string is "exception_filter", not "filter".

memorybroker.responsibility: Lightweight in-process topic-based pub/sub broker (no queue groups, no persistence, no ack/retry)

Message.description: Published message (no ID, no Metadata — removed in simplification)
fields: Timestamp time.Time - captured via time.Now() before dispatch

pattern_types: Exact: 'user.login' - O(1) map lookup, matches only that topic
Suffix: 'user.**' - O(1) map lookup by prefix; matches one or more segments below 'user.', not 'user'
Global: '**' - O(1), matches all topics. '*' is exactly one segment ('*' alone: single-segment topics); '**' is special only as the last segment; '>' is literal
Complex: 'user.*', 'user.*.profile', '*.created' - O(n) scan; segment-wildcard matching, NOT regex. Full table: internal/pattern/MATCHING.md
key_features: Single sync.RWMutex over 4 maps (exact/prefix/global/complex) - no sharding
PublishAsync: one goroutine per call tracked by sync.WaitGroup, no worker pool/bounded queue
Close(): CompareAndSwap-idempotent, waits for in-flight PublishAsync via WaitGroup, then clears all maps
Cross-broker Unsubscribe protection via ErrForeignSubscription (checks subscription.broker == receiver)
Unsubscribe(nil) is always nil, unconditionally, even after Close
Unconditional panic recovery per handler call (not configurable, no OnPanic hook)
publishInternal sizes handler slice exactly, skips allocation entirely when nothing matches

memorycache.responsibility: Bounded in-memory sharded byte cache with exact TTL and an atomic counter, no persistence

MemoryCacheOptions.description: MaxEntries int (default 65536, rounded down to a multiple of 64, minimum 64); MaxBytes int64 (default 16 MiB, minimum 64 KiB)

MemoryCache.description: In-memory cache, 64 shards with CLOCK eviction, bounded by MaxEntries and MaxBytes
constructors: NewMemoryCache(opts *MemoryCacheOptions) *MemoryCache - nil means the defaults; starts no goroutine and no timer
methods: Set(ctx, key string, val []byte, ttl time.Duration) error
SetNX(ctx, key string, val []byte, ttl time.Duration) (bool, error)
Incr(ctx, key string, delta int64, ttl time.Duration) (int64, error) - atomic 8-byte big-endian counter; a live counter keeps its expiry

notes: No file-based persistence anywhere in this package. Do NOT invent PersistenceConfig / NewMemoryCacheWithConfig — they do not exist and never have in current source.
There is no Stop method: the sweep is a time.AfterFunc armed only while an entry with a ttl exists, holding the cache through a weak.Pointer.
Errors: ErrEmptyKey, ErrNegativeTTL (negative ttl writes nothing), ErrEntryTooLarge (len(key)+len(val) > MaxBytes/64), ErrNotCounter.
hashKey uses hash/maphash with a random per-process seed — shard placement is stable within a process but not reproducible across restarts.
Eviction is CLOCK per shard: expired entries first, then live entries whose reference mark (set by a Get hit or a rewrite) is clear; marked entries get the mark cleared and are skipped.
key_characteristics: Sharded (64 shards, padded to cache lines) for concurrent R/W
Bounded: each shard holds MaxEntries/64 entries and MaxBytes/64 bytes; a full cache evicts, never fails
Monotonic-clock expiry; an expired entry is absent for every method before any sweep
No goroutine or timer while empty or when no entry expires

critical_rules: NEVER hold onto context after request completes
NEVER mutate context after guard stage
NEVER access raw websocket.Conn in handlers (use Publisher)
NEVER retain pooled objects beyond request lifetime
Code after next() runs before the next layer, not after the handler: post-handler work belongs in an interceptor's Pipe operators
Configuration methods (BindGlobal*, Enable*, SetLogger) only before Create
Providers are fields, never handler parameters
common_mistakes: Type mismatch between provider and handler parameter
Calling next() multiple times in middleware
Slow clients causing message drops in WebSocket
